criteria.statement: Every criterion the verification state file records as not `met` carries a `cause` taken from one fixed, enumerated set of causes
A criterion's `cause` survives a resume: a criterion settled in one run keeps the same `cause` when the next run carries it forward

A criterion that fails the deterministic evidence check is given a cause saying which way it failed — evidence missing, evidence stale, locator not found, and so on — distinct from a criterion whose evidence passed that check and which the Judge ruled failed
The causes distinguish, besides the evidence-check failures, at least: judged failed, environment not reachable, capability absent, and never exercised
The per-cause counts are computed from the stored `cause` field, never by pattern-matching the free-text reason

The report for a run ending `stalled`, `stuck`, `unbuilt` or `insufficient-coverage` carries a **Diagnosis** block directly under its Coverage line, giving a count per cause, and those counts agree with the per-criterion causes in the state file
The readout printed by `/verify-build`, and by `/implement-trd`'s verification step, on those same four outcomes gives the same diagnosis by cause with counts
On those four outcomes, both `/verify-build` and `/implement-trd` name the next step: a short chat with the bridge skill, then `/verify-build --fix`

The bridge skill, run as a short chat between the orchestrator and the owner, writes `.trd-state/<feature>/verification-plan.md` in a fixed shape with six parts: blockers (each small enough to be one task), slicing and order, owner rulings, criteria accepted as not verifiable, extra checks to add, and a stop rule
Owner rulings made in the bridge chat are written into the PRD or TRD as well as into `verification-plan.md`

The bridge skill ships to every project the way the check skills do: a freshly scaffolded project and an existing project after `--refresh` (and after a rebase) both have it in `.claude/skills/`, whatever `selected-skills.txt` says

The bridge skill is never selectable as a verification check: check selection in `/implement-trd`'s verification step, in `trd-authoring.md` and in the `/audit-trd` script never offers it, and a TRD naming it in `## Verification Artifacts` does not get it run as a check
The framework-shipped skills are declared in ONE list, where each entry has a role of `check` or `support`; the three verification check skills are `check` and the bridge skill is `support`

No reader of the framework skills keeps its own hand-copied set of names: the scaffold script, the three `rebase-project.md` copies, `trd-authoring.md`, the `/audit-trd` script, `/implement-trd`'s check selection, `packages/skills/README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and the runtime-integrity and scaffold tests each read or point to the one list

Adding a framework skill is a one-line edit to the list: a new entry with role `support` ships on scaffold and refresh with no other file changed, and a new entry with role `check` also becomes selectable as a verification check
`/verify-build` accepts `--fix`, with an optional plan path

A `--fix` round records each open `not_met` or `unbuilt` criterion, and each blocker in the plan, as a discovery row that blocks the feature; a row recorded for a criterion carries that criterion's id
Promoting discoveries to the TRD de-duplicates on criterion id: two discovery rows for the same criterion, worded differently, become one TRD row
`not_verifiable` criteria and an `insufficient-coverage` outcome are never turned into build tasks by `--fix`
With a plan that lists blockers, `--fix` builds the blockers before it runs its first re-verification
`--fix` builds through `/implement-trd --reconcile` in a chained mode that prints no `COMMAND COMPLETE` banner, sends no completion notification, and runs no functional verification of its own
Invoking `/implement-trd --reconcile` directly, not chained, still ends with its own banner and still runs verification by default
Each `--fix` round runs ONE fix batch covering everything that failed, then re-verifies only criteria still open; criteria already `met` are carried forward and not exercised again
After each `--fix` round the check pages are republished to their stored URLs, and the owner's comments on them are read before the next round begins
With a plan, `--fix` keeps repeating rounds until the plan's stop rule fires, and stops when it does

The stop rule is written in a small, fixed vocabulary that the bridge skill documents and `--fix` reads — for example a maximum number of rounds, stopping when a round closes fewer than N gaps, stopping when only blocked criteria remain
Without a plan, `--fix` runs exactly one fix-and-re-verify round, then reports
A plan that omits its stop rule still produces a bounded run: `--fix` applies a default stop rule and the readout says which one it applied

Without `--fix`, neither `/verify-build` nor `/implement-trd` goes beyond its one bounded verification loop: no gap is recorded as a build task, no build starts, and no fix is offered — the readout names the next step and the run ends
A `--fix` run asks the owner no questions from start to finish
When a `--fix` run stops, its report lists every criterion still not `met`, each with a reason
A `--fix` run, however many rounds it takes, ends with exactly ONE `COMMAND COMPLETE` or `COMMAND STUCK` banner, as its last line
An autonomous `--fix` run never edits `.claude/rules/verification.md`; a change it finds it needs is recorded for the next bridge chat instead

NG2 in `docs/TRD/verification-convergence.md` is amended, not deleted: it still exists and now cites the owner's reversal of 2026-09-27 and its two conditions — the outer loop runs only on explicit `--fix`, and it has one stop rule
`.claude/rules/process.md` and `packages/core/templates/process.md.template` say that `--verify` with `--resume` re-enters an **interrupted** verification loop, not a stalled one

`packages/core/commands/verify-build.md` no longer tells the user `--resume` picks up a run that "crashed, stalled, or was interrupted"; what it says `--resume` re-enters agrees with its own `--resume` section

`docs/TRD/functional-verification.md` and `docs/TRD/verification-convergence.md` place lane derivation at `/implement-trd` §8.1a, not §3.6a, and `functional-verification.md` says resume state is passed only when the resume flag was given explicitly and the prior run's outcome is unrecorded — not whenever a state file exists
`packages/core/lib/fix-plan.js` no longer says `--verify` is required when chaining into `/implement-trd`; its text agrees that verification is on by default
